title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector assistance to support vulnerable communities in drought and flood affected Moyale and Dubuluk Districts Borena Zone, Oromia

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="font-size: 8pt"gtAttribute to the five consecutive failed rainy seasons in the country and region, Borena zone experiencesnbspa severe drought which is far reaching as it wiped-outnbspHHs basic livelihood assets (livestock and crops).nbspFood shortage to human and livestock is apparent at the moment, affecting the most vulnerable groups, such as PLWs, children, elderly and poor households. Based on the ERP from Borena Zone on March 2023, 34,769 HHsnbspwere recorded destitute who parted with their livestock assets entirely. According to the zonal Inter-cluster coordination forum report, the Borena pastoralists have suffered an economic loss of 2,249,888 livestock (cattle alone) since October 28, 2022. About 39,500HH (221,200 persons) were displaced and sheltered within host communities in Borena zone. Out of this Dubuluk woreda consist of 8,989nbspdroughtsnbspaffected IDPs who require immediate assistance. In reference to the zonal ERP a total of 807,651 persons are in dire need of urgent water rationing and 102 water trucks are required along with the provision of 6,490 carton aqua tab. In addition, most of the motorized and hand pump wells have dried up indicating a need to replenish the water system. nbspMost importantly Livestock intervention is needed in the area in terms of animal drug supply, livestock vaccination, mass treatment and capacity building activities to strengthen animal healthnbspservice provision at community level. The need for provision of agricultural inputs (drought tolerant and fast maturing seeds andnbspagricultural hand tools) also needs due consideration. Considering the existing need in the ground and alignment with the agriculture cluster objective SO1 and SO2 ,the proposed project will prioritize key activities that contribute for agriculture production and livelihood restoration. Accordingly,nbspthe project will respond through the provision of supplementary livestock feed, livestock treatment and vaccination, distributions of agricultural inputs, MPC, as well as rehabilitation of water scheme for livestock use. Pertaining to the WASH response as indicated in the allocation paper and in the way to contribute for the WASH cluster objective SO1 and SO3, contextually proved activities such as distribution of WTC hygiene kits, promotion of proper water handling mechanism, construction of emergency semi-permanent latrines along with hand washing facilities at IDP sites in both Woredas will be prioritized. nbspAs an intermediate and long term,nbspthe project planned to rehabilitate non-functional Water schemes, that will provide safe drinking water for 11,500 individuals in two droughts affected woredas. This project will also deliver essential sanitation and hygiene messages through hygiene promotion for 50,000 people. Drought and cholera affected communities will be provided with basic lifesaving WASH NFIs such as bathing laundry soaps, water purification tabs and jerrycans and health facilities and schools will be supported benefiting 4,500 individuals. On the protection sector activities which is related to awareness raising on GBV and PSEA will be carried out to lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 8pt"gtnbsplt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 8pt"gtincrease the knowledge of the community members to reduce the prevalence of the GBV and SEA.nbspIn addition various lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 8pt"gtnbsplt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 8pt"gtcapacity building trainings on key concept of safeguarding , gender and PSEA will be provided to the project staffs and community members to minimize the probability of abuse committed by the staffs.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-size:8.0ptmso-bidi-font-size: 10.0ptfont-family:"gt ltbr style="mso-special-character:line-break"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-size:8.0ptmso-bidi-font-size:10.0pt font-family:"gtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gt
